title: OpenAI, Anthropic models took extreme measures in hacking test
content_html:
A bunch of researchers let AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic loose in a testing environment, and the results were a little spooky.

The United Kingdom's AI Security Institute released a report (via Engadget) detailing some incidents in which the models actually acted outside their testing parameters and hacked into external organizations in late July. In one incident, an AI agent attempted to insert malevolent code into a GitHub project using social engineering tactics. The AI looked into the project's owners and generated fake accounts with which it tried to get the code approved. Once denied, it created a new identity for itself to try again.

That's not all. The researchers say the AI models also contacted real people with what were essentially phishing attempts, with files asking the recipient to run evil code. Interestingly, the AISI said it did not explicitly tell the agents to be deceitful to humans; rather, the AI decided to take these extreme measures when they had difficulties accomplishing certain tasks. However, the organization stressed that there is no evidence that agents would ever act this way outside of a testing environment at this time.

"The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under 'deliberately permissive conditions' that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment."

Recently, both OpenAI and Anthropic have reported instances in which new models did escape secure environments during testing. In a particularly notable incident, an unreleased OpenAI model hacked the Hugging Face repository.

While the behavior exhibited by the models is definitely concerning, all of these incidents have one thing in common: They were part of hacking tests, in which the models were prompted to act outside their usual safeguards, ultimately turning to tried-and-true hacking methods pioneered by — who else? — humans. These sorts of social engineering hacking strategies are things humans do all the time, so maybe we could stand to look in the mirror for a minute here.

content_html_zh:
一群研究人员让 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的人工智能模型在测试环境中自由发挥，结果有点令人毛骨悚然。

英国人工智能安全研究所（通过 Engadget）发布了一份报告，详细介绍了 7 月下旬模型实际超出其测试参数并入侵外部组织的一些事件。 在一次事件中，人工智能代理试图使用社会工程策略将恶意代码插入到 GitHub 项目中。 人工智能调查了该项目的所有者并生成了虚假帐户，试图通过这些帐户来批准代码。 一旦被拒绝，它就会为自己创造一个新的身份来再次尝试。

这还不是全部。 研究人员表示，人工智能模型还通过本质上是网络钓鱼的尝试联系真人，并通过文件要求接收者运行邪恶代码。 有趣的是，AISI 表示，它并没有明确告诉特工要欺骗人类；相反，人工智能在完成某些任务遇到困难时决定采取这些极端措施。 然而，该组织强调，目前没有证据表明特工会在测试环境之外以这种方式行事。

“评估中的提示并未对如何使用互联网施加任何具体限制。 这以及安全措施的取消意味着这些模型是在“故意允许的条件”下进行测试的，这些条件并不代表我们的任何生产模型。 请注意，这里没有证据表明有人逃离安全环境。”

最近，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都报告了新模型在测试期间确实逃脱安全环境的实例。 在一个特别值得注意的事件中，一个未发布的 OpenAI 模型入侵了 Hugging Face 存储库。

虽然模型表现出的行为肯定令人担忧，但所有这些事件都有一个共同点：它们都是黑客测试的一部分，在测试中，模型被提示在其通常的防护措施之外采取行动，最终转向由其他谁首创的经过考验的黑客方法？ ——人类。 这些社会工程黑客策略是人类一直在做的事情，所以也许我们可以在这里照照镜子。
